units.translation: Thus M, not κρατεῖταί πως [is it somehow ruled], which the editors wrote. κρατεῖ δέ πως [but somehow it rules] Elmsley on Eur. Med. 50. Thus M, for which I wrote δὸς δ᾽ ἔπ᾽ [but grant upon]. Most fitting would be δὸς τελεσφόρον κράτος [grant power that brings fulfillment].

where Weil wrote κράτος [power] quite plausibly. For although κράτεσιν ἀρσένων [by the powers of men] is read in this very play at v. 393, here there was no reason why he should add to the singular νίκη [victory] the plural κράτη [powers], which could have been introduced by a scribe straying to the ending of the preceding word. Similarly Plato Leg. 12 p. 962 said νίκην καὶ κράτος τῶν πολεμίων [victory and power over the enemies], and Demosth. p. 381, 12 κράτος πολέμου καὶ νίκην [power of war and victory].
